character: 2.54-mile (4.10km) undulating Georgia road course with dramatic elevation change and the famous Esses sequence. Rhythm through the fast, blind sections and a strong exit from Turn 10b onto the back straight are critical.

corners.name: Turn 1
corners.type: fast downhill right-hander with a compression point
corners.technique: Commit through the blind downhill entry, let the car settle in the compression
corners.trap: Braking too late on the downhill approach and running wide

corners.name: The Esses
corners.type: fast, flowing left-right-left combination (Turns 4-5) with big elevation change
corners.technique: Rhythm and smooth inputs, carry maximum speed through the sequence
corners.trap: Over-driving any single apex disrupts the whole sequence

corners.name: Turn 10a
corners.type: tight right-hander after a short straight from the Esses
corners.trap: Carrying too much speed in and running out of track

corners.name: Turn 10b
corners.type: quick left immediately after 10a, feeds the back straight
corners.technique: Late apex, prioritise exit speed above all — the second most important corner on the track
corners.trap: Compromising the exit here costs time down the entire back straight
